title: Roundabouts & Mini-Roundabouts
whatItIs: Use MSM at every stage, give priority to traffic from the right unless told otherwise, and pick lane and signals by your exit.
keyFacts: Decide your exit early and time signals so they don't confuse others.
Give priority to traffic from the right, unless signs, markings or lights say otherwise.

keyFacts.text: At a mini-roundabout you MUST pass round the central markings (except large vehicles that can't).

keyFacts: Mini-roundabouts are normally on roads with a 30 mph limit or less. Avoid U-turns at them.
Give priority to cyclists on the roundabout; don't overtake them within their lane.

routes.label: 1st exit · turning left
steps: Signal left, approach in the left lane

routes.label: 3rd exit · turning right
steps: Signal right, approach in the right lane

notes: Unless signs or markings show otherwise (rule 186)

a.label: DT1: normal driving
points: Fault: cutting across the normal position

b.label: DT1: lane discipline
points: Fault: straddling or leaving your lane

onTheTest.question: Your pupil is taking the 3rd exit (right). When should they signal left?
onTheTest.why: Rule 186: signal left after you pass the exit before the one you want. DT1 records late exit signals.

onTheTest.question: A cyclist in the left lane of a roundabout is signalling right. What does it most likely mean?
onTheTest.why: Rule 186: cyclists and horse riders may stay in the left lane, signalling right to show they are not leaving. Don't cut across them.

traps: Markings let you enter without giving way? Still look right first.
Others may not signal correctly or at all: watch their position.
Long vehicles may straddle lanes: give them plenty of room.
